Preliminary

/prih-LIM-uh-ner-ee/ — rhymes with ordinary · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Preliminary means coming before, and preparing for, something more important; introductory.

Such preliminary work, the architect explained, always comes long before the detailed blueprints that engineers actually build from.

Worked Example

Before approving the new campus building, the university required architects to conduct preliminary research on the site, studying soil and checking local building codes.

Preliminary is more precise than 'early'—it describes work that comes before something more important and exists specifically to prepare for it. The research isn't just early in time; it's preparatory work that must happen before the main blueprints can be drawn.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

introductory: coming first simply to introduce something

preparatory: focused purely on getting things ready

opening: merely first, without preparing anything larger

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

final: coming last, with nothing following after

culminating: forming the peak everything built toward

Where it sits · how much it paves the way — opening → introductory → preparatory → preliminary

opening vs. preliminary: The opening act of a variety show merely comes first and entertains on its own; opening says nothing about preparing the way for something more important.

introductory vs. preliminary: An introductory paragraph welcomes readers into an essay, but it only introduces; preliminary work, like the rough outline drafted beforehand, exists so the real essay can be built from it.

preparatory vs. preliminary: A scientist's preparatory wiping-down of the lab bench gets everything ready, but preparatory stops at readiness; preliminary adds that the step comes before — and clears the way for — the main experiment.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pre- (prae-)

Prefix — pre- (prae-): before

Root — limin-

Root — limin-: threshold (from Latin limen, liminis — the strip you cross to enter a doorway)

Suffix — -ary

Suffix — -ary: relating to, connected with

Put it together

Put it together: Pre- (before) + limin- (threshold) + -ary (relating to) builds the meaning literally: relating to what happens before the threshold — the steps taken before you cross into the main event. A preliminary round, meeting, or exam is the doorway you pass through on the way to the real thing. Latin limen, 'threshold,' also gives English limit — the line you don't cross.

Use the root in a new word: subliminal

Use the root in a new word: subliminal: The advertisement contained a subliminal message that viewers absorbed without consciously noticing it.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / neutral

Preliminary is used when something is preparation for something more important—preliminary reports, preliminary research, preliminary rounds. For things that just happen to be first without being specifically preparatory, simpler words like 'opening' or 'first' often work better.
